produced_by: mentat/app/graph.js:writeScope (called from refresh(), the one path every Graph control change reaches)
consumed_by: S6 (inherits this vocabulary for the pane model: evidence, id, committee, offset, limit)
description: The console's URL scheme. The hash names the tab (app.js showView) and the query string carries the scope, so a permalink, a reload and a tab switch are one operation. Values are encodeURIComponent-encoded and decoded with URLSearchParams; keys are plain. write() merges into the live query: an empty value removes its key, unknown keys are preserved in place, existing keys keep their order and new keys append. A value write() would refuse is never put in the URL, so anything read() rejects could only have been typed by hand. Tab switches stay on history.replaceState (Paul's ruling C); pushState is never used. Orientation only - the examples are the contract.

industry.value: The published industry label exactly as the snapshot registry lists it (S4 HANDOFF: 'Credit Union', 'Property & Casualty Insurance'). Any non-empty string; the label, never the slug. URL-encoded, so '&' survives.
writers: mentat/app/chart-studio.js (dataset picker, Open in Chart Studio)

company.value: Company name as the Graph company select spells it. Any non-empty string.

cycle.value: Election-cycle END year, four digits, as Graph spells it (2024). Chart Studio translates it to the index's pair spelling with chart-studio-core.js carriedFilterValue('cycle', value).

mode.value: One of direct, activity, estimates - the #graph-mode option values. 'direct' is the default and is removed from the URL rather than written.

direction.value: A #graph-direction option value. 'Support' is the default and is removed.

tier.value: A #graph-tier option value (Chief, Middle-Management, Employees, Unknown). Empty means all levels and is removed.

funding.value: A #graph-funding option value. 'all' is the default and is removed.

category.value: The recipient-type drill-down id Graph holds in its module-level `category`.

recipient.value: The organization drill-down id Graph holds in its module-level `recipient`.

saved.value: A 32-character lowercase hexadecimal saved-view id, the same shape server.py save_view() mints (uuid4().hex) and get_view() demands (re.fullmatch(r'[a-f0-9]{32}')).

studioPane.value: PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by S5: B, C or D selects a Chart Studio comparison pane's localStorage store (chart-studio.js:17). scope.js never writes it and never removes it - it is one of the unknown keys write() preserves in place.
writers: the reader, by hand, and chart-comparison.js's pane frames

reserved_note: S6's pane model owns these keys. S5 writes none of them and its write() merge preserves any that are present, exactly as it preserves studioPane.

examples.name: graph_permalink_downstream_activity
examples.why: Ruling A(ii): mode=activity is linkable, and the Candidate view select is visible as soon as a report is chosen.

examples.name: chart_studio_permalink
examples.why: Company and cycle arrive as carried filter pills through pendingScope/applyGraphScope.

examples.name: saved_view_permalink
examples.why: saved= opens one saved view through the existing openability()/openView() path.

examples.name: cross_reference_permalink
examples.why: S4's GET /api/cross-reference?industry=<label> selects the newest run for a label.

examples.name: ampersand_label
examples.why: A published label with '&' in it must survive the round trip; this is why values are encodeURIComponent'd rather than handed to URLSearchParams.toString().

examples.name: graph_filters_full
examples.why: Every Graph filter key at once, in the serialization order scope.js writes.

examples.name: write_merge_remove_on_empty_and_preserve_unknown
examples.why: The two write() rules in one example: an empty value removes its key, an unknown key (studioPane, S6's future keys) is preserved untouched and keeps its place. Existing keys keep their order; a new key appends.

negative_controls.why: mode=pac is not a #graph-mode option value. A bad permalink must still open the tab, so the key is dropped and reported rather than thrown.

invalid.reason: mode must be one of direct, activity, estimates

negative_controls.why: A two-digit cycle is not the four-digit end year Graph spells.

invalid.reason: cycle must be a four-digit election-cycle end year

negative_controls.why: A non-numeric cycle is refused by the same rule, so the shape of the refusal cannot depend on the value happening to be digits.

invalid.reason: cycle must be a four-digit election-cycle end year

negative_controls.why: An explicitly blank industry is not a scope. It is dropped and reported; the rest of the URL still reads.

invalid.reason: a blank value names no scope, so the key is dropped

negative_controls.why: saved=xyz is not 32 hex, which is exactly what server.py get_view() refuses. The client must not fire a request the server will answer 400 for.

invalid.reason: saved must be a 32-character hexadecimal saved-view id

negative_controls.why: The teeth of the other five: a URL with no query at all invents nothing. An empty scope and an empty invalid[] - not a default industry, not a default mode. This is the control that fails if read() ever starts guessing values the reader did not put in the URL.
